title: Electrical Engineer, Specialist
description:
Today’s most tomorrow company.

We built the world’s most powerful battery, the 850MW Waratah Super Battery, and now we need more technical experts to help us on our mission.

We are leading the energy transition towards a better, brighter tomorrow. The work you will do makes a real and very tangible impact on the future of the planet and its people. We’re 200 people around the world with 40 GWh of projects moving through development across Australia, Japan, the US and Germany.

Akaysha build, own, and operate our assets, we don’t hand a project to someone else once it’s approved. The people who design a battery site are the same people who build it and run it for the next twenty years.

You’ll join our Development Engineering team, and act as one of our technical experts on BESS and PCS Technologies. You will drive decisions play a key role in shaping Akaysha's approach to technology procurement across its international project portfolio.

What you'll do

  • Lead the technical direction of utility-scale BESS projects, from design reviews through to Investment Committee approval.
  • Own OEM engagement, supplier selection and contract technical evaluations across batteries, PCS and key project technologies.
  • Drive techno-commercial assessments, pricing strategies and bid responses that shape the future of our portfolio.
  • Build and maintain the engineering tools, standards and technical governance that enable Akaysha to scale globally.

How you'll make a positive impact

  • Deep expertise in BESS technology, project design and engineering risk management.
  • Commercial judgement that balances technical performance, project risk and investment outcomes.
  • The ability to turn complex technical information into clear recommendations for executives, investors and stakeholders.
  • A passion for emerging technologies and the energy transition, with the credibility to influence suppliers, partners and project teams.

Why you’ll love working here

  • Flexibility first: we're hybrid by design, averaging 60/40 office and home split, and real trust to flex that mix when life calls for it.
  • Room to look after yourself: $1,500 a year for your wellbeing, plus $2,000 and two extra days off for your own development.
  • Genuinely generous parental leave: because family isn’t something you fit around a job
  • A stake in what we build: on top of your salary and twice-yearly bonus, permanent team members also share in the value we create through our Long Term Incentive Plan.

Lead the energy transition with us. Apply now.

We believe diverse teams build better solutions for the planet and its people. We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and able to do their best work, no matter their background, identity, or lived experience.

What you’ll do

  • Lead Group budgeting, rolling forecasts and strategic planning across the business
  • Turn month-end into Executive and Board reporting that shapes the next decision, and the future of the business
  • Partner with Investments and Treasury on the calls that decide where we grow next
  • Help rebuild how FP&A works day to day, so it keeps pace as we move into new markets

How you’ll make a positive impact

  • A knack for turning a dense set of numbers into a story a Board will act on

title: Senior Grid Connnection Engineer
description:
Today’s most tomorrow company.

We run the most powerful battery on the grid, the 850MW Waratah Super Battery, and getting the next ones connected is your job.

We are leading the energy transition towards a better, brighter tomorrow. The work you will do makes a real and very tangible impact on the future of the planet and its people. We’re 200 people around the world with 40 GWh of projects moving through development across Australia, Japan, the US and Germany.

We build, own, and operate our assets, we don’t hand a project to someone else once it’s approved. The people who design a battery site are the same people who build it and run it for the next twenty years.

You’ll lead our connection applications end to end, from first enquiry through to registration, working closely with Commercial and Engineering to get the settings right from day one.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the Connection Application process end to end, including Connection Enquiries, Generator Performance Standards, design and modelling packages, validation, Hold Point testing and registration submissions
  • Work with Business Developers and Engineering to optimise project designs, equipment selection and grid connection planning
  • Liaise directly with OEMs, external consultants and AEMO/NSPs, troubleshooting power system models and control system performance
  • Negotiate technical performance standards with AEMO and NSPs, balancing our long-term operation of the asset against regulatory requirements
  • Keep across new rules and regulations, and help shape our responses to proposed changes

How you’ll make a positive impact

  • A degree in Electrical, Control or Power Systems Engineering
  • Hands-on experience in renewables or electrical engineering, ideally on utility-scale or power transmission projects
  • Solid knowledge of NEM grid connection processes and Australian engineering standards
  • Comfort with power system modelling tools like PSSE, PSCAD or PowerFactory

Why you’ll love working here

  • Flexibility first: we're hybrid by design, averaging 60/40 office and home split, and real trust to flex that mix when life calls for it.
  • Room to look after yourself: $1,500 a year for your wellbeing, plus $2,000 and two extra days off for your own development.
  • Genuinely generous parental leave: because family isn’t something you fit around a job
  • A stake in what we build: on top of your salary and twice-yearly bonus, permanent team members also share in the value we create through our Long Term Incentive Plan.
